They are primarily located in states adjacent to the Canadian provinces of Ontario and Québec, with a few locations also in Texas and Georgia.
clues.summary: The most popular chain in Canada, but with many US locations too, mostly in states bordering Ontario and Quebec, plus a few in Texas and Georgia.

clues.title: Restaurant: In-N-Out Burger
text: ‘**In-N-Out Burger**’ is a regional fast food chain located primarily in the Southwest US. Around two thirds of all locations are located in California.
clues.summary: A regional fast food chain in the Southwest, with about two thirds of the locations in California.

clues.title: Gas station: Wawa
text: ‘**WaWa**’ is a regional gas station and convenience store chain with locations in the Mid-Atlantic states and Florida. New Jersey and the Philadelphia, Pennsylvania area have the highest density of locations.
clues.summary: A regional gas station and convenience store chain in the mid-Atlantic states and Florida, densest in New Jersey and the Philadelphia area.

clues.title: Gas station: Sheetz
text: Another regional gas station and convenience store chain in the Eastern US is called ‘**Sheetz**’. Most of their locations are in the Mid-Atlantic and Central Appalachian areas of the US. Pennsylvania has the highest number of locations.
clues.summary: A regional gas station and convenience chain in the mid-Atlantic and central Appalachians, with the most in Pennsylvania.

clues.title: Gas station: Kwik Trip
text: ‘**Kwik Trip**’ is a chain of gas stations and convenience stores that are located in the Upper Midwest states of Wisconsin and Minnesota. In Iowa, these stores are called ‘[**Kwik Star**](https://goo.gl/maps/6MgdfZ1ey134z9Yi6)’ and have similar branding. Some stores may also have the name ‘[Stop-N-Go](https://maps.app.goo.gl/KXXGnVPs4aBiXU39A)’.
clues.summary: A gas station and convenience chain in Wisconsin and Minnesota. In Iowa it is called Kwik Star with similar branding, and some are called Stop-N-Go.

clues.title: Gas station: Kum & Go
text: ‘**Kum & Go**’ is a regional gas station chain based out of the state of Iowa. They also have pockets of locations in the Ozarks, Colorado, Wyoming, and North Dakota.
clues.summary: A gas station chain based in Iowa, with pockets in the Ozarks, Colorado, Wyoming and North Dakota.

clues.title: Gas station: Casey's
text: ‘**Casey’s**’ is a popular gas station and convenience store chain that is found in the Midwest, Plains, and parts of the Mid-South. Illinois, Iowa, and Missouri have the highest number of locations.
clues.summary: A popular gas station and convenience chain in the Midwest, Plains and parts of the Mid-South, with the most in Illinois, Iowa and Missouri.

clues.title: Gas station: Buc-ee's, huge with many pumps
text: ‘**Buc-ee’s**’ is a small chain of oversized gas stations located primarily in the state of Texas. These stores feature multiple rows of gas pumps, and a very large convenience store building.
NOTE: Some other nearby states have Buc-ee’s locations, but they are quite rare outside of Texas.
clues.summary: An oversized gas station with many rows of pumps and a very large store. Mainly in Texas, rare in nearby states.

clues.title: Plate: all-yellow, or yellow with orange circle
text: The most common and recognisable Alaskan licence plate is **all yellow**. In Generation 4 coverage you can also get a plate with a large orange circle in the middle. Front plates are required in Alaska.

images.caption: Alaska plates from three eras: 2010 onwards, 2015 onwards and 1997-2004

clues.summary: The most common plate is all yellow. In Gen 4 you may also see one with a large orange circle in the middle. Front plates are required.

clues.title: Sign: highway shield with the Big Dipper
text: The Alaskan highway shield has an image of the **Big Dipper constellation** on the bottom left.

images.caption: A highway shield with the Big Dipper stars, above a North plate

clues.summary: The highway shield has the Big Dipper constellation at the bottom left.

clues.title: Trees: thinner, narrower-leaved than elsewhere
text: Trees in Alaska are generally **thinner** and have less broad leaves than those seen in the other 49 states.
clues.summary: Trees are generally thinner and have less broad leaves than those in the other 49 states.

clues.title: Coverage: tall snow-covered mountains in view
text: On a lot of the Alaskan coverage you will be able to see tall, **snow covered mountains**.
clues.summary: Much of the coverage shows tall, snow-covered mountains.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 2 is fairly common here
text: In most of the US, Generation 2 is rare. However, Alaska has a fair amount of **Generation 2 coverage**.
clues.summary: Gen 2 is rare across the US, but Alaska has a fair amount.

clues.title: Google car: low camera, big round blur
text: Alaska has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front, with the front of the white car being very visible. The blur can also be fully transparent.

images.caption: Four panels labelled front panned down, front panned straight, back panned down and good blur (front)

clues.summary: A Gen 4 "smallcam" mounted lower than usual, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front, and the front of the white car clearly visible. The blur can be see-through.

clues.title: Google car: low-quality older camera
text: Alaska is the only state in the US where **shitcam** **coverage **is prevalent. This coverage is lower resolution with more faded colours, compared to other camera generations. Also, a large blur can be seen at the bottom of the page.
clues.summary: Alaska is the only state with plenty of older low-resolution coverage with faded colours and a large blur at the bottom of the image.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 4 near the largest city
text: **Generation 4** coverage in Alaska is concentrated around the city of **Anchorage**.
clues.summary: Gen 4 coverage is concentrated around the largest city, Anchorage.

clues.title: Vegetation: subarctic, little undergrowth
text: Most of interior and northern Alaska lies in subarctic or** tundra** climate zones. These areas feature relatively low amounts of [forest undergrowth](https://maps.app.goo.gl/mFe2xNzxYnqgY5Af6) and [shorter trees](https://maps.app.goo.gl/oaa8n8a7AbYVj7YSA).
clues.summary: Most of the interior and north is subarctic or tundra: little undergrowth in the forest and shorter trees.

clues.title: Landscape: tall green forested mountains
text: The Alaskan towns in the Alexander Archipelago, on the British Columbia border have a unique look. Tall mountains with **lush green forests** can be seen in the background, with the majority of buildings made of wood. In addition, [Generation 2](https://goo.gl/maps/YU3fykwkkhwSeihP8) coverage is often overcast and misty.
NOTE: Coastal areas of [Oregon](https://goo.gl/maps/JUuhjUojP42eQrsF7) and [Washington](https://goo.gl/maps/LikUSJBshaMjidcK6) can have a similar appearance in terms of landscape and foliage.
clues.summary: Towns in the southeastern archipelago near the British Columbia border: tall mountains with lush green forest behind, mostly wooden buildings, and often overcast, misty Gen 2. Coastal Oregon and Washington can look similar.

clues.title: Cities: only two major urban areas
text: The only two major **urban areas** in Alaska are Anchorage and [Fairbanks](https://maps.app.goo.gl/kGD8vrgWHiQVVy73A).

images.caption: A city street with only two major urban areas in the state

clues.summary: The only two major urban areas are Anchorage and Fairbanks.

clues.title: Suburbs: wide roads, commercial strips
text: Most of the **suburban areas** in Alaska are in and around Anchorage.These areas feature wide roads, commercial districts, and sometimes heavy traffic. Mountains can commonly be seen in the distance.
NOTE: Fairbanks has some [similar areas](https://maps.app.goo.gl/y5zA5uE8KjngyPVV8), but mountains are less prevalent.
clues.summary: Most suburbs are around Anchorage, with wide roads, commercial areas, sometimes heavy traffic and mountains in the distance. Fairbanks has similar areas but fewer mountains.

clues.title: Trees: aspen, white bark and round leaves
text: **Aspen trees** ([Populus tremuloides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Populus_tremuloides)) can be found in lower elevation areas of interior and south-central regions of Alaska. These trees have white bark and rounded leaves.
clues.summary: Aspens grow at lower elevations in the interior and south-central areas. White bark, rounded leaves.

clues.title: Fields: farmland only in the far south
text: Due to Alaska’s very cold climate; **agricultural fields** are mainly found in the south of the state, mostly in the Matanuska Valley and Kenai Peninsula.

images.caption: Farmland in a flat field beside the road

clues.summary: Because of the cold, farm fields are mainly in the south, in one valley and on one peninsula.

clues.title: Pipeline: big oil pipeline beside main roads
text: The **Alaskan pipeline** which is usually visible from main roads, can be seen at these points. This is an easy way to identify Alaska as there are no similar pipelines in the rest of the US.

images.caption: A big oil pipeline on supports beside the main road

clues.summary: The Alaska pipeline is usually visible from main roads. There is no similar pipeline anywhere else in the US.

clues.title: Landscape: built-up town ringed by forested mountains
text: **Juneau**, Alaska’s Capital city, is the largest settlement in the Alaskan panhandle. Therefore, it is much more ‘built up’ than other towns in this area. The city is surrounded by heavily forested mountains and hills.
clues.summary: The capital is the largest town in the panhandle and much more built up than the others, surrounded by heavily forested mountains and hills.

clues.title: Fire hydrants: pale pink or pale yellow
text: Fire hydrants in Anchorage are typically** pale pink **or** pale yellow** in colour.

images.caption: A pale pink fire hydrant on a sidewalk

clues.summary: Fire hydrants in the largest city are typically pale pink or pale yellow.

clues.title: Fire hydrants: bright yellow or multicoloured
text: Fire hydrants in Fairbanks are commonly either** bright yellow **or a** combination of colours** (most commonly [yellow and blue](https://maps.app.goo.gl/akUtjiVdnQMo9emy6)).

images.caption: Bright yellow and blue-topped fire hydrants

clues.summary: Fire hydrants in the second city are bright yellow or a mix of colours, most often yellow and blue.

clues.title: Google car: low-quality camera only near two cities
text: **Shitcam** is only found around Anchorage and Fairbanks, and parts of the road that connects them.
NOTE: This map shows all places where this camera can be found. Keep in mind coverage may be updated in some places, therefore you may come across regular coverage in places highlighted here.
clues.summary: The older low-quality camera is only found around the two big cities and parts of the road between them. Some places may have been updated.

clues.title: Landscape: flat, snowy, overcast
text: The North end of the Dalton Highway features a **flat** and **snowy landscape** and an overcast sky. A [small ridge](https://goo.gl/maps/fNWJxvvpz1Jzwjs89) of hills can be seen to the west of the highway in certain spots.
clues.summary: The north end of a long northern highway is flat and snowy under overcast sky, with a small ridge of hills to the west in places.

clues.title: Road: gravel highway in Gen 2 with wildflowers
text: The Denali highway, stretching from Cantwell to Paxson in central Alaska, is a mostly **gravel highway** in the ‘Alaska’ mountain range. This road runs generally east to west, is covered in the generation 2 camera, and was taken in late summer, so wildflowers and green shrubby plants are common.
clues.summary: A mostly gravel highway across central mountains running east to west, in Gen 2 shot in late summer, so wildflowers and green shrubs are common.

clues.title: Road: gravel highway in Gen 2, lower mountains
text: The Steese Highway is another gravel highway that goes from Fairbanks to the town of ‘Central.’ Similar to the Denali highway, this road runs generally east to west and is covered in generation 2. The difference, however, is that the **mountains** along this road are noticeably **lower** than the ones adjacent to the Denali Highway.
clues.summary: Another gravel highway running east to west in Gen 2, like the previous one, but with noticeably lower mountains alongside.

clues.title: Road: foggy rainy weather in Gen 2
text: Highway 5, from the Yukon border to Tetlin Junction, can be recognized by the **foggy, rainy** weather, and Generation 2 camera.

NOTE: The Top of the World Highway on the Canadian side also has similar weather, but is mostly paved and has no outer lines, unlike the American side, which is only paved west of Chicken, and does have outer lines.
clues.summary: A highway from the Yukon border is recognised by foggy, rainy weather in Gen 2. The Canadian side nearby has similar weather but is mostly paved and has no outer lines.

clues.title: Landscape: cold dead land, overcast
text: Prudhoe Bay, the northernmost town in America covered by street view, can be recognized by **cold, dead** landscape, overcast clouds and lack of tall buildings. A second Google car can sometimes be seen.
clues.summary: The northernmost town covered: a cold, barren landscape under overcast sky with no tall buildings. A second Google car is sometimes visible.

clues.title: Coverage: three isolated towns, backpack only
text: [Nome](https://goo.gl/maps/efqLHvNVtEK2fGPNA), [Unalakleet](https://goo.gl/maps/1DYUKxvbEs7sR17v5) and [Galena](https://goo.gl/maps/aX2axEUDjqNexfiR6) are three isolated Alaskan towns which are covered only by trekker. The trekker’s **lime green hat** or [black and white beanie](https://goo.gl/maps/V28pqftM9fbJ8Qwo6) can be seen.
NOTE: The trekker’s black and white bandana can only be seen in Nome.
clues.summary: Three isolated towns are covered only by backpack camera. The carrier's lime green hat or black-and-white beanie shows; the black-and-white bandana appears only in one of them.

clues.title: Plate: white with rainbow arc
text: The most common Hawaii licence plate is **white** with an **arcing rainbow** across the centre of the plate. When blurred, you can sometimes see the outline of the rainbow. Front plates are required in Hawaii.
clues.summary: The most common plate is white with an arcing rainbow across the middle, sometimes visible through the blur. Front plates are required.

clues.title: Language: Hawaiian, 8 consonants and okina
text: Hawaii is the only state to use its own language, though English is still predominantly used. Most **place names** are in Hawaiian, so you can spot it on street signs, and other road markers.
- Hawaiian is a vowel-oriented language that only uses eight consonants: H, K, L, M, N, P, W, and (ʻ), called an [ʻOkina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%CA%BBOkina).
- Every Hawaiian word ends in one of 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, or U.
- Each vowel can also have a [macron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macron_(diacritic)) over it: Ā, Ē, Ī, Ō, and Ū.
These vowels are often combined to make [Diphthongs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diphthong). I.e. UI, AI, AE, etc...
clues.summary: The only state with its own language, though English dominates. Place names are Hawaiian, using only H, K, L, M, N, P, W and the ʻokina. Every word ends in a vowel, and vowels may have a macron.
